chunks: 1762 - It is narrated from Masʿadah ibn Ṣadaqah, from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, from his forefathers عليهم السلام:

Indeed, Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام sent to a man five awsuq of dates from al-Bughaybighah. The man was among those who hoped for his voluntary generosity, was content with his gift and support, and did not ask anything from ʿAlī عليه السلام or anyone else. Then a man said to Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام, 'By Allah, so-and-so did not ask you for anything, and one wasq out of the five awsuq would have been enough for him.'

So Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام said to him: 'May Allah not increase your kind among the believers. I give, while you are miserly with it. If I do not give to the one who hopes in me except after his asking me, and then I give him after the asking, then I have only given him the price of what I took from him. That is because I exposed him to offering me his face, which he places in the dust before my Lord and his Lord, Mighty and Majestic, at the time of his worship of Him and his asking Him for his needs.'

So whoever does this to his Muslim brother, while knowing that he is a proper recipient of his charity and kindness, has not been truthful to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, in his supplication for him, when he wishes Paradise for him with his tongue yet is miserly toward him with the trifles of his wealth.

That is because a servant may say in his supplication: 'O Allah, forgive the believing men and the believing women'; so when he supplicates for him with forgiveness, he has indeed asked Paradise for him.
So unfair is the one who does this in speech but does not make it real through action.'

key_terms.أَوْسَاقٍ: large measured quantities used here for dates
key_terms.الْحُطَامِ: the trifling, perishable goods of worldly wealth
key_terms.مَسْأَلَتِي: my being asked; the act of requesting from someone
key_terms.نَوَافِلَهُ: his voluntary generosity and extra acts of giving

ai.seo_question: Why is giving to the needy before they ask considered superior in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that true generosity is to give before a needy believer is forced to ask, preserving his dignity and honor. Amir al-Muʾminin عليه السلام condemns the contradiction of praying for believers with one’s tongue while withholding material help from them in practice.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1762 - Mas’ada ibn Sadaqa narrates from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as), from his forefathers (as):

"Indeed, the Commander of the Faithful (as) sent to a man five wasaq (measures) of dates from al-Bughaibigha. This man was among those who would hope for his generosity, appreciate his kindness, and be content with what he gave. He would not ask anything of Ali (as) or anyone else.
A man said to the Commander of the Faithful (as), 'By Allah (swt), so-and-so did not ask you for anything, and one wasaq would have sufficed him from the five wasaqs.'

The Commander of the Faithful (as) replied to him: 'May Allah (swt) not increase among the believers those like you. I give, and you are miserly with it. If I do not give to the one who hopes for me except after he asks me, and then I give it to him after he has asked, then I have only given him the price of what I have taken from him. That is because I have subjected him to sacrifice his dignity for me, which he places in the dust before his Lord (azj) and my Lord (azj), the Almighty, in his devotion to Him and his request for his needs from Him.
Whoever does this to his Muslim brother, knowing that he is deserving of his kindness and support, has not been truthful with Allah (swt), the Almighty, in his supplication for him.

This is when he prays for him, saying: "O Allah (swt), forgive the believers, male and female." By this supplication, he is asking for Paradise for him. How unfair is he who prays with his tongue but does not support it with action, withholding the trivial wealth of this world from him.
That is because the servant may say in his supplication, "O Allah (swt), forgive the believers, male and female." When he supplicates for his forgiveness, he is asking for Paradise for him.
Thus, he is not fair who does this with his words but does not fulfill it with his deeds.'"
